name: Alexisonfire
label: Distort Entertainment
lede: Five kids from St. Catharines took their name from a porn star's website, put three singers on one record and sold platinum in Canada. They broke up badly in 2011, then came back with an album, thirteen years after the last one, that won a Juno.

eras.title: Three bands fold, five kids regroup
eras.text: In St. Catharines, Ontario, three local bands broke up at the same time and their survivors pooled into one. Alexisonfire had a clean singer, a screamer and a guitarist who did both, and a following that spread by word of mouth faster than the distribution deal could keep up.

years.h: Three St. Catharines bands break up at once, and the survivors regroup
years.p: George Pettit (Condemning Salem), [[Dallas Green|06b65c62-b894-45ec-88f4-b7d689851e35]] (Helicon Blue), Wade MacNeil and Chris Steele (Plan 9) and drummer Jesse Ingelevics pool what's left of their old groups.
years.xp: They billed themselves as the sound of two Catholic high-school girls in mid-knife-fight. The vocals split three ways: Green sang clean, Pettit screamed, MacNeil did both.

years.h: Alexis Fire threatens to sue; the name turns out to be free
years.p: The band took its name from the website of adult performer Alexis Fire. She threatened legal action, but the name wasn't a registered trademark and nothing came of it.

years.h: A demo wrapped in the drummer's math homework gets them signed
years.p: Recording engineer Greg Below and Montreal journalist Mitch Joel heard Jesse Ingelevics' Math Sheets Demo while starting a label, Distort Entertainment, and signed the band.

years.h: Alexisonfire lands on Halloween
years.p: The self-titled debut comes out on Distort, with EMI distributing in Canada. Word of mouth did most of the selling, per Wikipedia, and it went gold in Canada in October 2005.

years.h: Two Canadian crossings, Hellfest, and Europe with Rise Against
years.p: Alexisonfire tour Canada twice with [[Billy Talent|fd429857-5ace-4609-ae54-1502c3bdac11]] and Spitalfield and play Hellfest, after earlier Ontario and New York runs with [[Gwar|f7ccd53a-234c-4800-8d1b-21b201bad1de]] and [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]].

eras.title: Gold in twelve weeks
eras.text: Watch Out!, made in producer Julius Butty's home studio near Hamilton, took Alexisonfire from word of mouth to the charts, and Equal Vision brought it to the US. Then the drummer left, and Dallas Green started a quiet solo project that would change everything.

years.h: Watch Out! debuts at No. 6 in Canada
years.p: It sells 6,580 copies in its first Canadian week, goes gold in twelve weeks and platinum by 2007. Equal Vision releases it in the US three weeks later.

years.h: "Pulmonary Archery" wins Best Video at the Canadian Independent Music Awards
years.p: The same year, the CASBY Awards name Alexisonfire Favourite Indie Band.

years.h: Alexisonfire win a Juno as New Group of the Year
years.p: The 2005 Juno comes with a second prize: the "Accidents" video wins Best Independent Video at the MuchMusic Video Awards.

years.h: Jesse Ingelevics quits, and Jordan Hastings of Jersey takes over drums
years.p: The band spends the rest of 2005 on the road with its new drummer, including Reading and Leeds and Japan's Summer Sonic.

years.h: Dallas Green starts a folk side project called [[City and Colour|b1003bf1-25b8-41f4-a783-36060f987913]]
years.p: A quiet solo record project that becomes a hit in its own right and, six years later, one of the reasons Alexisonfire breaks up.

eras.title: A boat on the Thames, then 300 dates
eras.text: Crisis made Alexisonfire one of the biggest bands in Canada and a festival draw in the UK and Australia. The follow-up came out on a label run by their old manager, and under all that touring the band was coming apart.

years.cap: Crisis, 2006: the cover draws on the Great Lakes blizzard of 1977
years.h: Crisis goes in at No. 1 in Canada
years.p: The third album sells more than 20,000 copies in its first Canadian week and goes platinum by May 2007. The launch party is on a boat on the Thames in London.
years.xp:
Recorded at Metalworks in Mississauga and Silo Recording in Ontario in early 2006 with Julius Butty. Gared O'Donnell of [[Planes Mistaken for Stars|ff428f12-1c80-4437-bfff-0e9af6ff94c9]] sings on "You Burn First", and the title track draws on the Great Lakes blizzard of 1977. In the US it came out on Vagrant Records, not Equal Vision.

A ten-month world tour followed, with Reading and Leeds, Festival d'été de Québec and a headline night at Brixton Academy. Kerrang! later ranked Crisis 50th on its list of the 50 greatest albums of the 21st century.

yt: "This Could Be Anywhere in the World" official video
years.h: Best Cinematography for "This Could Be Anywhere in the World"
years.p: The MuchMusic Video Awards prize arrives the same year Alexisonfire are nominated for Group of the Year at the Junos. The single goes gold in Canada in 2018.

years.cap: Wade MacNeil on stage at Warped Tour, July 2009
years.h: Wade MacNeil says the band hasn't split, just reached a crossroads
years.p: Breakup rumors run through the next year while Dallas Green sketches heavier, weirder songs that later come out as the Dog's Blood EP.
years.xp: George Pettit once said the band wanted to kill screamo rather than save it, a line Wikipedia notes he later regretted. The four-song Dog's Blood EP was sketched in 2008 and released in 2010.

years.cap: Dallas Green on stage at Warped Tour, July 2009
years.h: Alexisonfire sign to Dine Alone, a label run by their old manager
years.p: Joel Carriere, the band's former manager, founded Dine Alone Records. Recording of Old Crows / Young Cardinals had started on February 1.

years.h: Old Crows / Young Cardinals starts a tour of about 300 dates
years.p: The fourth album has "Young Cardinals" as its single. The touring runs to December 2010.

years.h: Seconds into a free Olympics show, the crowd breaks the barrier
years.p: At an all-ages show at Live City Yaletown during the Vancouver Winter Olympics, the rush of the audience takes the barrier down and people are trampled. About 20 are slightly injured.

years.cap: George Pettit at Soundwave Festival, Australia, February 2010
years.h: The hometown show nobody knew was the last
years.p: Alexisonfire close the Old Crows / Young Cardinals tour at home. Dallas Green later treats it as the band's final concert.

eras.title: Not amicable
eras.text: Dallas Green's City and Colour had grown too big to share his time, and Wade MacNeil had an offer to front a British punk band. The split was ugly enough that the farewell had to wait a year.

years.h: A tweet promises an album so heavy Dog's Blood will sound like ska
years.p: Alexisonfire say they're writing a fifth record. Six months later the band is over.

years.cap: George Pettit on stage at Warped Tour, July 2009
years.h: Alexisonfire end it, and George Pettit says it wasn't friendly
years.p: Pettit announces the breakup, citing Green's and MacNeil's exits and personal issues among the rest. Green left to focus on [[City and Colour|b1003bf1-25b8-41f4-a783-36060f987913]], MacNeil to front the UK band [[Gallows|4cb159df-bd09-4f42-bfec-09b6a248a52f]].
years.xp: Green said he'd had a nervous breakdown and that being in Alexisonfire was killing him. Pettit described the split as not amicable. A planned tenth-anniversary Canadian tour and a run of releases were dropped.

years.big: nobody knew it was our last show
years.h: Dallas Green wants a goodbye the band didn't get in 2010
years.p: Green, on why he and Wade MacNeil are talking about one last run: the real final show, in Hamilton two years earlier, went by unannounced.

years.cap: Alexisonfire in Vancouver on the farewell tour, December 2012
years.h: Death Letter re-cuts songs from all four albums
years.p: The EP lands as the farewell tour begins. The tour grows from nine dates to 30, across Canada, the UK, Australia and Brazil.

years.h: The farewell ends at Copps Coliseum in Hamilton
years.p: Billed as the last show. The recording comes out in 2016 as Live at Copps, on four records and a Blu-ray.

eras.title: Officially back
eras.text: The farewell lasted two years. Alexisonfire returned as a part-time band, one singer now a professional firefighter, and when the new album finally came it won them a Juno.

years.h: 1,000 vinyl boxes vanish in 30 minutes on Christmas Day
years.p: The set holds all four albums plus EPs and B-sides. A slightly smaller second edition follows in August 2014.

years.h: Alexisonfire book their first shows since the farewell
years.p: The list includes Reading and Leeds, Heavy Montréal and Riot Fest.

years.h: Wade MacNeil tells Riot Fest Toronto the band is officially back
years.p: The band later clarifies it has "no immediate plans" for new music or tours.

years.h: Fans brighten three black Instagram images and find a release date
years.p: The numbers 2, 15 and 19 point to "Familiar Drugs", the band's first new material in nearly nine years.

years.h: George Pettit has been a firefighter since 2015
years.p: He tells the Toronto Star the job comes first, even with Alexisonfire back together.

years.h: Thirteen years on, Otherness
years.p: Announced March 10 and released on Dine Alone, it's the first album of new studio recordings since 2009. It wins Rock Album of the Year at the 2023 Junos.

years.h: Alexisonfire cover [[The Tragically Hip|e86ab653-bec8-46f3-b4b6-a1a866919ef6]]'s "Fully Completely"
years.p: It's on Copies of Old Masters, Vol. 1, a covers EP on Dine Alone.

years.h: "Dogs of Chernobyl" debuts as the new album is called done
years.p: Alexisonfire make the announcement at a Crisis 20th-anniversary show at RBC Amphitheatre, after recording since February.
